subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden `NO_REPLY` suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and what boundary should separate silent-intent/internal text from legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main intentionally preserves some substantive trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to prevent internal text leaks; that is a shared message-delivery and security-boundary choice rather than a mechanical cleanup close.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define and test a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies across delivery paths.

options.title: Use blanket trailing or own-line suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` token, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the current narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-wrapped, JSON, and reasoning-prefixed silent payloads are suppressed, then retarget broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define and test a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies across delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans shared reply delivery, compatibility, and security policy; steipete has central-file history and is the best available routing candidate from the likely owners.
